comparisons.peer_topic: AI Software Ecosystem and Silo AI Acquisition
comparisons.peer_summary: To support its AI strategy, AMD consolidated AI teams to develop a comprehensive software ecosystem, improved AMD ROCm software performance, and acquired Silo AI Oy to accelerate AI model development and deployment on AMD hardware, leveraging Silo's software stack for training large language models.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD are actively expanding their AI software ecosystems to complement their hardware, though they focus on different layers of the stack. AVGO emphasizes infrastructure software for cloud environments (mainframe/hybrid cloud) to manage complexity, while AMD focuses on the AI software stack (ROCm) and acquiring AI labs (Silo AI) to accelerate model deployment on its specific hardware accelerators. AVGO's strategy targets broader IT environment management, whereas AMD's is tightly coupled to optimizing performance for generative AI workloads on its silicon.

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions help enterprises simplify their information technology environments so they can increase business velocity and flexibility, and enable customers to plan, develop, deliver, automate, manage and secure applications across mainframe, distributed, edge, mobile, and private and hybrid cloud platforms.
To execute our AI strategy, we brought together multiple AI teams across AMD to drive development of a comprehensive software ecosystem spanning our full product portfolio.
The acquisition of Silo AI enables customers to accelerate development and deployment of AI models on AMD hardware.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD agreed to acquire ZT Group Int'l, Inc. (ZT Systems) in August 2024 to extend data center infrastructure capabilities and accelerate time to market for AI solutions, with expected closure in the first half of fiscal 2025 subject to regulatory approvals and intent to seek a strategic partner for ZT's manufacturing business.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and AMD both utilize acquisitions to extend their data center infrastructure capabilities, but with different strategic end-games. AVGO's portfolio includes infrastructure software and connectivity for data centers, implicitly supporting the broader ecosystem. AMD explicitly acquired ZT Systems to extend 'data center infrastructure capabilities' and accelerate time-to-market for AI solutions, indicating a push into hardware infrastructure assembly and integration, whereas AVGO's description focuses on designing and supplying the underlying semiconductor and software solutions.

sentences.text: We are a global technology leader that designs, develops and supplies a broad range of semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions.
We develop semiconductor devices with a focus on complex digital and mixed signal complementary metal oxide semiconductor based devices and analog III-V based products.

We also focused on extending our data center infrastructure capabilities by entering into an agreement in August 2024 to acquire ZT Group Int'l, Inc. (ZT Systems), a provider of AI and general purpose compute infrastructure for hyperscale computing companies.
We believe that with the acquisition of ZT Systems, we can accelerate time to market for our leadership AI training and inferencing solutions.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel is leading the shift to run networking workloads in software through network function virtualization, offering efficient and programmable platforms, and works with over 500 ecosystem partners to help enterprises optimize their networks.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and INTC both address enterprise networking, but their approaches differ significantly. AVGO offers fiber channel storage area networking products and infrastructure software to simplify IT environments, positioning itself as a broad semiconductor and software provider. INTC is leading the shift to 'run networking workloads in software' via network function virtualization (NFV), focusing on creating programmable, software-defined platforms. AVGO's description highlights hardware and software breadth for connectivity and storage, while INTC's is specific to virtualizing network functions on its platforms.

sentences.text: We develop semiconductor devices with a focus on complex digital and mixed signal complementary metal oxide semiconductor based devices and analog III-V based products.

Our infrastructure software solutions help enterprises simplify their information technology environments so they can increase business velocity and flexibility, and enable customers to plan, develop, deliver, automate, manage and secure applications across mainframe, distributed, edge, mobile, and private and hybrid cloud platforms.

We are leading the world's shift to run networking workloads in software and create network function virtualization to provide our customers with more efficient, cost-effective, and programmable platforms that enable secure, agile, and reliable networking solutions from edge to cloud.

comparisons.peer_topic: Network and Edge solutions strategy and target markets
comparisons.peer_summary: Intel's network and edge solutions aim to provide edge-optimized, AI-enabled compute and connectivity to move networks to software infrastructure. These solutions serve developers building distributed edge infrastructure and applications across verticals including industrials, federal, aerospace, retail, healthcare, education, and smart cities.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and INTC both serve the edge and cloud continuum with AI-enabled solutions. AVGO explicitly lists 'data center servers and storage systems' and 'edge' in its product applications, while INTC specifically targets 'distributed edge infrastructure' and 'edge AI' across verticals like industrials and healthcare. Both companies align on the trend of moving intelligence to the edge, but AVGO frames this within a broader consumer and enterprise hardware portfolio, whereas INTC frames it as a specific network and edge compute strategy to move networks to software infrastructure.

sentences.text: We offer thousands of products that are used in end products such as enterprise and data center networking, including artificial intelligence ("AI") networking and connectivity, home connectivity, set-top boxes, broadband access, telecommunication equipment, smartphones and base stations, data center servers and storage systems, factory automation, power generation and alternative energy systems, and electronic displays.

Our network and edge solutions aim to unleash the power of intelligent edge solutions for our customers and move the world's networks to a software infrastructure that runs on Intel technologies by providing edge-optimized, AI-enabled compute and connectivity solutions to run every workload at the edge, between the cloud and the end user, and deploying software platforms that enable developers to build, deploy, run, manage, connect, and secure distributed edge infrastructure, applications, and edge AI across several verticals, such as industrials, federal, aerospace, retail, healthcare, education, and smart cities.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company experienced substantial improvements in pricing and margins in 2024, driven by increased demand growth partly from AI deployment, normal customer inventories, and industry supply discipline.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and MU both discuss the impact of AI on their respective market conditions, but from different angles. MU reports that AI deployment drove demand growth that improved pricing and margins in 2024, contrasting with previous year weakness. AVGO positions its AI networking and data center products as core parts of its portfolio without citing specific pricing dynamics driven by AI in this specific text. While both recognize AI as a demand driver, MU provides specific financial outcome evidence (pricing/margin improvement), whereas AVGO provides strategic product positioning.

sentences.text: We develop semiconductor devices with a focus on complex digital and mixed signal complementary metal oxide semiconductor based devices and analog III-V based products.
Throughout 2024, we experienced substantial improvements in pricing and margins.

Increasing demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI and mostly normal customer inventories, combined with industry-wide supply discipline, resulted in an industry supply and demand balance that substantially improved from 2023 conditions.

comparisons.peer_topic: Data Center Segment Financial Performance and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 increased 217%, driven by strong demand from enterprise software, consumer internet applications, and industry verticals like automotive, financial services, and healthcare, with compute revenue up 244% and networking revenue up 133%.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and NVDA both identify AI and Data Centers as core market drivers. AVGO describes its products as used in 'enterprise and data center networking, including artificial intelligence ("AI") networking' and infrastructure software for cloud platforms. NVDA provides specific financial context, stating Data Center revenue increased 217% driven by AI infrastructure demand. Both companies treat AI networking and data center compute/networking as primary growth vectors, with AVGO focusing on the connectivity/software layer and NVDA on the compute/acceleration layer within the same Data Center segment.

sentences.text: We develop semiconductor devices with a focus on complex digital and mixed signal complementary metal oxide semiconductor based devices and analog III-V based products.

Our infrastructure software solutions help enterprises simplify their information technology environments so they can increase business velocity and flexibility, and enable customers to plan, develop, deliver, automate, manage and secure applications across mainframe, distributed, edge, mobile, and private and hybrid cloud platforms.
Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2024 was up 217%.
Data Center compute revenue was up 244% in the fiscal year.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA specializes in computing platforms that provide acceleration for applications across four large markets: Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive, incorporating processors, interconnects, software, and services.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and NVDA both describe their business as providing computing platforms or solutions for key industry markets. AVGO defines itself as designing 'semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions' used in data center servers, storage, and AI networking. NVDA specializes in 'computing platforms' addressing Data Center, Gaming, and other markets. Both disclosures frame their strategy around providing the foundational hardware and software platforms that enable end-user applications in these large markets.

sentences.text: We are a global technology leader that designs, develops and supplies a broad range of semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions.

We offer thousands of products that are used in end products such as enterprise and data center networking, including artificial intelligence ("AI") networking and connectivity, home connectivity, set-top boxes, broadband access, telecommunication equipment, smartphones and base stations, data center servers and storage systems, factory automation, power generation and alternative energy systems, and electronic displays.
We specialize in markets where our computing platforms can provide tremendous acceleration for applications.
Our platforms address four large markets where our expertise is critical: Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization, and Automotive.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm believes that 5G, combined with high-performance computing and on-device AI, will drive adoption in automotive and IoT sectors, and that maintaining leadership in 5G technology development, standardization, and IP licensing is critical for long-term business sustainability.
comparisons.comparison: AVGO and QCOM both address the convergence of computing technologies with AI in specific sectors like automotive. AVGO lists 'factory automation' and connectivity products used in 'smartphones and base stations' as part of its broad semiconductor portfolio, while QCOM explicitly believes '5G combined with... on-device artificial intelligence' will drive adoption in automotive and IoT. Both recognize the expansion of their connectivity/computing technologies beyond traditional core markets (smartphones for QCOM, general connectivity for AVGO) into adjacent sectors powered by AI and 5G.

sentences.text: We develop semiconductor devices with a focus on complex digital and mixed signal complementary metal oxide semiconductor based devices and analog III-V based products.

We believe that 5G combined with high-performance, low-power computing and on-device artificial intelligence will continue to drive adoption of certain technologies that are already commonly used in smartphones by industries and applications beyond mobile handsets, such as automotive and IoT.
